outcomes: Use advanced grammar and vocabulary to demonstrate oral competence in the Spanish language and compose and present well-structured oral presentations in Spanish expressing complex ideas. (Communication, Critical Thinking, Self-Awareness and Interpersonal Skills).

Interpret, analyze, and summarize Spanish-language advanced level texts orally and in writing according to their cultural, literary and/or linguistic content. (Communication, Critical Thinking, Global Awareness and Valuing Diversity).
Use advanced grammar and vocabulary to compose well-constructed critical essays in Spanish with special emphasis on stylistics, form, content, purpose, and style. (Communication, Critical Thinking).

Distinguish, compare, and contrast the different elements of the cultures of Spain and the Hispanic world, including basic history, literature, and art; assess Hispanic contributions to the global society, and the role of the Spanish language and heritage in various parts of the world.
Design and execute a project that examines and evaluates a special topic.

notes: Course codes printed with leading zeros (e.g., SPANISH 001) match closed-list codes without them (SPANISH 1).
List A says 'Select 1 course' but prints three 'or' pairs; recorded each pair as one entry with its alternative and minimum 1 course.

Course Substitutions block applies only to students who placed out of required courses; it sets no fixed unit count of its own, only that the major reach a minimum of 18 units total, so minimum is left null. Unused List A courses may also serve as substitutions.
Catalog notes the prerequisite for SPANISH 036 is SPANISH 035 (a substitution course), not SPANISH 002.
Degree total recorded from 'Total Minimum Units: 60' printed under this award; Cal-GETC 34 semester units recorded as ge_units.
